metadata.title: ITEA Framework: A Multidimensional System for Measuring Occupational Exposure to Algorithmic Expropriation under the Agentic AI Regime
metadata.description:
The ITEA Framework provides ten complementary indicators covering 1,016 SOC 6-digit occupations from O*NET 30.2, designed to measure occupational exposure to algorithmic expropriation in the Agentic AI regime, distinct from but complementary to task-level automation indices in the Frey-Osborne tradition or ability-based exposure measures such as the AIOE benchmark of Felten, Raj and Seamans (2021).

Version 3.0 introduces three major methodological revisions motivated by a documented case study of three research papers (the trilogy 8A/8B/8C): (1) z-score ITEA aggregation, (2) IRA with triple residualisation against GEE, ITEA and ICT, and (3) a dual-variant OAEI architecture (multiplicative canonical and additive alternative). The release also unifies the prior operational v1.x and methodological v2.x numbering lines onto a single semantic version, archiving v1.45 as the v1.45-legacy tag for replication.

External convergent validation against the AIOE benchmark of Felten, Raj and Seamans (2021): r(OAEI v3.0+, AIOE) = 0.797 over 738 common SOC 6-digit occupations.

This Zenodo record archives the complete repository, including reference implementations in R and Python, a 14-test pytest suite reconciling code output against the canonical workbook within machine precision, the Consolidated Methodology document, multilingual READMEs (EN/ES/PT/ZH), the JOSS paper draft, and a SHA-256 manifest for integrity verification.
references: Felten, E. W., Raj, M., & Seamans, R. (2021). Occupational, industry, and geographic exposure to artificial intelligence: A novel dataset and its potential uses. Strategic Management Journal, 42(12), 2195–2217.
Frey, C. B., & Osborne, M. A. (2017). The future of employment: How susceptible are jobs to computerisation? Technological Forecasting and Social Change, 114, 254–280.
Bollen, K., & Lennox, R. (1991). Conventional wisdom on measurement: A structural equation perspective. Psychological Bulletin, 110(2), 305–314.
Nonaka, I., & Takeuchi, H. (1995). The Knowledge-Creating Company. Oxford University Press.
